name: Mountains of Ararat
note: Scripture names only the 'mountains of Ararat' (the land of Urartu); the pin is the traditional peak, Mount Ararat in eastern Turkey.

events.q: Upon which mountains did Noah's ark come to rest after the flood?
On which mountains did the ship carrying Noah's sons Shem, Ham and Japheth come to rest?

name: Babylon
note: The ruins of Babylon lie beside the Euphrates near Hillah, Iraq; tradition links the Tower of Babel in the land of Shinar with this city.

events.q: In which city of the land of Shinar did people build a tower 'whose top reaches to the sky' until the LORD confused their language?
In the province of which city did Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refuse to worship the golden image and survive the fiery furnace?
In which city did a hand write on the palace wall during Belshazzar's feast?
By the rivers of which city did the exiles sit down and weep, hanging their harps on the willows?
In which city did Evilmerodach release King Jehoiachin from prison and seat him at his table for life?
To which city did the Assyrian captains carry King Manasseh in chains, where he humbled himself and prayed?
When Nebuchadnezzar carried Judah away, to which city did the priest Jehozadak go into captivity?
In which land of exile did the captive king Jechoniah become the father of Shealtiel?

name: Ur of the Chaldees
note: Usually identified with Tell el-Muqayyar in southern Iraq, though some scholars have argued for a northern Ur near Harran.

events.q: From which city of the Chaldeans did Terah set out with Abram, Sarai, and Lot toward Canaan?

name: Haran
note: The ruins of Harran survive near the modern village of Harran in southeastern Turkey.

events.q: Where did Terah die, before Abram departed at the LORD's call at age seventy-five?
Toward which city was Jacob traveling, to the house of Laban, when he fled from Esau?

name: Nineveh
note: The mounds of Nineveh (Kuyunjik and Nebi Yunus) stand within modern Mosul, Iraq.

events.q: Which great city repented in sackcloth after Jonah preached that it would be overthrown in forty days?
In which Assyrian capital was Sennacherib struck down by his own sons while worshiping in the house of Nisroch?
In which city of exile did Tobit bury the dead of his people in secret?

name: Susa (Shushan)
note: The citadel of Susa is an excavated mound beside the modern town of Shush in southwestern Iran.

events.q: In which Persian royal citadel did Esther risk her life by approaching King Ahasuerus uninvited?
Where was Nehemiah serving as the king's cupbearer when he wept over news of Jerusalem's broken walls?
Where was Daniel, beside the river Ulai, when he saw the vision of the ram and the male goat?
In which Persian citadel did the king and Haman sit down to drink while the city was thrown into confusion by the decree against the Jews?

name: Ecbatana
note: Ancient Ecbatana, capital of Media, lies beneath modern Hamadan, Iran (the hill of Hegmataneh).

events.q: In which city of Media did Tobias marry Sarah, daughter of Raguel, after the demon was driven away?
In the palace of which Median city was the scroll of Cyrus's decree to rebuild the Temple found?

name: Rages
note: Rages (Rhagae) is identified with Rey, now on the southern edge of Tehran; the ancient city's exact core is debated.

events.q: To which city of Media did Raphael travel to collect from Gabael the silver Tobit had left in trust?

name: River Chebar (near Nippur)
note: The Chebar is thought to be the Kabaru canal near Nippur in southern Iraq, known from Babylonian tablets; its exact course is uncertain.

events.q: Beside which river among the exiles did Ezekiel see the heavens opened and the living creatures and wheels?

name: Carchemish
note: The ruins of Carchemish lie on the Euphrates at the Turkey–Syria border near Jarabulus.

events.q: At which city on the Euphrates did Nebuchadnezzar defeat the army of Pharaoh Necoh?

name: Shechem
note: Shechem is the excavated mound of Tell Balata on the eastern edge of modern Nablus.

events.q: Where did Abram first build an altar in Canaan, by the oak of Moreh, after the LORD promised the land to his offspring?
Where did Simeon and Levi kill the men of the city to avenge their sister Dinah?
Where did Joshua gather all the tribes and declare, 'As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD'?
Where did all Israel gather to make Rehoboam king, only for the ten tribes to reject him?

name: Bethel
note: Generally identified with the Palestinian village of Beitin north of Jerusalem, though a few scholars prefer nearby el-Bireh.

events.q: Where did Jacob dream of a stairway reaching to heaven with angels ascending and descending on it?
Where, besides Dan, did Jeroboam set up a golden calf for the northern tribes to worship?
At which royal sanctuary did the priest Amaziah order the prophet Amos to go back to Judah?
Which city, with Jeshanah and Ephron, did King Abijah capture from Jeroboam?
Where was the ark kept, with Phinehas ministering before it, when Israel wept and asked whether to fight Benjamin again?

name: Ai
note: Commonly identified with et-Tell near Deir Dibwan, but the site shows no occupation in Joshua's era, so nearby Khirbet el-Maqatir is a rival candidate.

events.q: Which city defeated Israel's first attack because Achan had taken devoted things from Jericho?
Which city did Joshua take with an ambush, after signaling with his outstretched javelin?

name: Oaks of Mamre
note: The traditional site is Ramat el-Khalil (Elonei Mamre) just north of Hebron, where Herod and later Constantine built enclosures.

events.q: By which oaks was Abraham sitting at his tent door when three visitors came and promised Sarah a son?

name: Hebron (Cave of Machpelah)
note: The Cave of the Patriarchs, enclosed by a Herodian wall, still stands in the center of Hebron.

events.q: Where did Abraham buy a burial cave from Ephron the Hittite to bury Sarah?
Where was David anointed king over the house of Judah after Saul's death?
In which city did Absalom have himself proclaimed king in rebellion against his father?
Where did Esau and Jacob bury their father Isaac, who died there at a hundred and eighty years old?
Where did Jacob tell his sons he had buried Leah, asking to be laid there with his fathers?

name: Beersheba
note: Biblical Beersheba is Tel Be'er Sheva, an excavated mound east of the modern Israeli city.

events.q: Where did Abraham and Abimelech swear an oath over a disputed well, and Abraham plant a tamarisk tree?
Where did Jacob offer sacrifices and hear God say, 'Don't be afraid to go down into Egypt'?
To which southern town of Judah did Elijah flee from Jezebel, leaving his servant there?
In which wilderness did Hagar wander with Ishmael until God opened her eyes to see a well?

name: Gerar
note: Usually identified with Tel Haror in the western Negev, though Tel Abu Hureira's identification is not certain.

events.q: Where did Isaac reopen his father's wells and quarrel with local herdsmen over Esek and Sitnah?

name: Sodom
note: Its site is unknown; tradition places it at the southern end of the Dead Sea (others propose Bab edh-Dhra or Tall el-Hammam to the north).

events.q: In which city did Lot take in two angels, before fire and sulfur rained down and his wife became a pillar of salt?

name: Mount Moriah (Temple Mount)
note: Scripture places the Temple on Mount Moriah (2 Chr 3:1); identifying it with the mountain of Isaac's binding is an ancient tradition.

events.q: To which mountain did God send Abraham to offer up his son Isaac?
On which mountain, at Araunah's threshing floor, did Solomon begin building the house of the LORD?
Where did the twelve-year-old Jesus stay behind, sitting among the teachers asking questions?
Where did Isaiah see the Lord enthroned with seraphim crying 'Holy, holy, holy' in the year King Uzziah died?
Where did the priest Jehoiada crown the boy king Joash, while Athaliah tore her clothes and cried 'Treason!'?
Where did Zerubbabel and Jeshua set the priests and the sons of Asaph praising as the foundation of the rebuilt temple was laid?
Where did the high priest Hilkiah find the book of the law, which Shaphan the scribe then read to King Josiah?
Where did King Jotham build the upper gate of the LORD's house?

name: Peniel (Penuel)
note: Penuel is usually placed at Tulul edh-Dhahab on the Jabbok (Zarqa) River in Jordan; the identification is probable, not certain.

events.q: Where did Jacob wrestle with a man until daybreak and receive the name Israel?

name: Dothan
note: Tel Dothan is an excavated mound in the northern West Bank, southwest of Jenin.

events.q: Where were Joseph's brothers pasturing the flock when they threw him into a pit and sold him?
Where did Elisha pray that his servant's eyes be opened to see horses and chariots of fire on the mountain?

name: On (Heliopolis)
note: On (Heliopolis) is in the northeastern suburbs of Cairo, where a single obelisk still stands at Matariya.

events.q: Whose priest Potiphera gave his daughter Asenath to Joseph as wife?

name: Land of Goshen
note: Goshen was a district of the eastern Nile Delta, probably around the Wadi Tumilat and the region of modern Faqus; its borders are not precisely known.

events.q: In which land did Pharaoh settle Jacob's family so they could pasture their flocks?
Which land where the Israelites lived was spared from the plague of flies?
Into which land did Jacob's household of seventy, including Perez and his sons Hezron and Hamul, come when they went down into Egypt?
In which land of Egypt was Jacob living when he crossed his hands to bless Ephraim above Manasseh?

name: Raamses (Pi-Ramesses)
note: Raamses is probably Pi-Ramesses at Qantir and Tell el-Dab'a in the eastern Delta; the companion store-city Pithom is likely Tell el-Maskhuta or Tell er-Retaba.

events.q: Which store city, along with Pithom, did the enslaved Israelites build for Pharaoh?
From which city did the Israelites set out on foot toward Succoth on the night of the Passover?

name: Red Sea crossing
note: The crossing site is unknown (proposals range from the Bitter Lakes to the Gulf of Aqaba); the pin follows the old tradition at the head of the Gulf of Suez.

events.q: Where did Moses stretch out his hand so that the waters divided and Israel crossed on dry ground?
After the waters returned over Pharaoh's army, where did Miriam take a tambourine and sing, 'the horse and his rider he has thrown into the sea'?

name: Mount Sinai (Horeb)
note: The true mountain is uncertain; since at least the 4th century tradition has placed it at Jebel Musa, where St. Catherine's Monastery stands.

events.q: Where did Moses see a bush burning that was not consumed?
On which mountain did the LORD descend in fire and speak the Ten Commandments?
While Moses was on which mountain did Aaron make the golden calf below?
On which mountain did Elijah hear the LORD not in the wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a gentle whisper?
In which wilderness did the LORD have Moses count the Levites, the clans of Gershon, Kohath and Merari?
In which wilderness did Nadab and Abihu die offering strange fire, leaving Eleazar and Ithamar to serve as priests?
On which mountain did Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and seventy elders see the God of Israel and eat and drink?

name: Tahpanhes
note: Usually identified with Tell Defenneh in the northeastern Delta near the Suez Canal.

events.q: In which Egyptian town did Jeremiah bury large stones at Pharaoh's palace, foretelling Nebuchadnezzar's throne there?

name: Alexandria
note: Founded by Alexander the Great, the ancient city lies beneath modern Alexandria on Egypt's Mediterranean coast.

events.q: In which city was Apollos, the eloquent Jew mighty in the Scriptures, born?

name: Midian (Al-Bad')
note: Midian was a region of northwest Arabia east of the Gulf of Aqaba; local tradition at Al-Bad' (Maghair Shuaib) marks the home of Jethro.

events.q: To which land did Moses flee from Pharaoh, where he defended seven sisters at a well and married Zipporah?

name: Kadesh Barnea
note: Most scholars identify it with the oasis of Ein el-Qudeirat in northeastern Sinai, near the Egypt–Israel border.

events.q: To which wilderness camp did the twelve spies return carrying a cluster of grapes on a pole?
Where did Miriam die and was buried, before Moses struck the rock instead of speaking to it?

name: Ezion Geber
note: Ezion Geber lay at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba near Eilat; Tell el-Kheleifeh is the usual but disputed identification.

events.q: At which port beside Eloth on the Red Sea did Solomon build a fleet of ships?

name: Mount Nebo
note: Jebel Nebo (Siyagha) in Jordan, with its Franciscan memorial church, has borne the name since antiquity and fits the biblical description.

events.q: From which mountain did Moses view the whole Promised Land before he died?

name: Kir Hareseth
note: Kir Hareseth, capital of Moab, is generally identified with Kerak in Jordan, beneath the Crusader castle.

events.q: On whose city wall did the king of Moab sacrifice his eldest son as a burnt offering, so that Israel withdrew?

name: Rabbah of the Ammonites
note: Rabbah is the Citadel hill (Jabal al-Qal'a) in the center of Amman, Jordan.

events.q: During the siege of which Ammonite city was Uriah the Hittite placed in the fiercest fighting and killed?

name: Ramoth Gilead
note: Usually placed at Tell er-Rumeith in northern Jordan near Ramtha, though the identification is not certain.

events.q: At which city was King Ahab killed by an arrow shot at random, despite his disguise?
Where did a young prophet sent by Elisha anoint Jehu king of Israel?

name: Bethany beyond the Jordan
note: The traditional baptism site is Al-Maghtas on the east bank opposite Jericho (a UNESCO site); the exact place is not certain.

events.q: Where was Jesus baptized by John when the Spirit descended like a dove?
Where was John baptizing when he pointed out Jesus as 'the Lamb of God'?
Near which river crossing, by tradition, was Elijah taken up by a whirlwind in a chariot of fire?

name: Jericho
note: Old Testament Jericho is Tell es-Sultan beside the modern city; New Testament Jericho lay just southwest at Tulul Abu el-Alayiq.

events.q: Whose walls fell after Israel marched around the city for seven days and shouted?
Where did Zacchaeus climb a sycamore tree to see Jesus?
Leaving which city did Jesus give sight to blind Bartimaeus?
Whose bad water did Elisha heal by throwing salt into the spring?
In the plains of which city did the Chaldean army overtake the fleeing King Zedekiah?

name: Gibeon
note: Gibeon is el-Jib, north of Jerusalem, where jar handles inscribed with the city's name and a great rock-cut pool were found.

events.q: Whose inhabitants tricked Joshua into a treaty by wearing worn-out sandals and carrying moldy bread?
Over which city did Joshua command the sun to stand still?
Where did Solomon offer a thousand burnt offerings and ask God in a dream for an understanding heart?
By whose pool did twelve men of Abner and twelve of Joab's men fight and all fall together?
At which high place did David leave Zadok and his fellow priests to minister before the LORD's tabernacle?

name: Beth Horon
note: Upper and Lower Beth Horon are the villages of Beit Ur al-Fauqa and al-Tahta on the old ascent road northwest of Jerusalem.

events.q: Down which ascent did Joshua pursue the Amorites while the LORD threw great hailstones on them?
At which ascent did Judas Maccabeus, with a small company, rout the Syrian commander Seron?

name: Hazor
note: Tel Hazor in the Upper Galilee is a UNESCO-listed excavated mound, the largest in the region.

events.q: Which city, 'the head of all those kingdoms,' did Joshua burn with fire?
From which city did Jabin, king of Canaan, oppress Israel with Sisera as his commander?

name: Shiloh
note: Shiloh is Khirbet Seilun in the central West Bank, an excavated site with a visitor center.

events.q: Where did Israel set up the tent of meeting after the land was subdued?
Where did Hannah pray so fervently for a son that Eli thought she was drunk?
Where did the boy Samuel hear the LORD calling him by night?

name: Mount Tabor
note: The isolated dome of Mount Tabor rises over the Jezreel Valley; the Gospels do not name the Mount of the Transfiguration, which tradition has identified with Tabor since the 4th century.

events.q: On which mountain did Barak gather ten thousand men before descending on Sisera's chariots?
On which high mountain, by long tradition, was Jesus transfigured before Peter, James, and John?

name: Spring of Harod
note: Usually identified with Ein Harod (Ma'ayan Harod) at the foot of Mount Gilboa, now a national park.

events.q: At which spring did Gideon choose his three hundred men by how they drank the water?

name: Timnah
note: Timnah is probably Tel Batash in the Sorek Valley.

events.q: On the way to which Philistine town did Samson tear apart a young lion with his bare hands?

name: Gaza
note: Ancient Gaza lies beneath the old city of modern Gaza on the Mediterranean coast.

events.q: From which city did Samson carry off the doors of the gate up to a hilltop?
In which city did the blinded Samson bring down the house of Dagon on the Philistines?

name: Gibeah
note: Gibeah of Saul is usually identified with Tell el-Ful in north Jerusalem, though some prefer nearby Jaba'.

events.q: In which Benjamite town did the Levite's concubine suffer the outrage that led to civil war?
To which hometown did Saul return after being chosen king, accompanied by men whose hearts God had touched?

name: Aphek (Antipatris)
note: Tel Afek at the source of the Yarkon River was Herod's Antipatris; identifying the Aphek of 1 Samuel 4 with it is probable.

events.q: Near which Philistine camp was the ark of God captured and Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas killed?
Where did Paul's military escort halt by night on the way from Jerusalem to Caesarea?

name: Ashdod
note: Tel Ashdod lies south of the modern Israeli port city of the same name.

events.q: In which Philistine city did the statue of Dagon fall face down before the captured ark?

name: Beth Shemesh
note: Tel Beth Shemesh is an excavated mound in the Sorek Valley beside the modern city of Beit Shemesh.

events.q: To which town did two milk cows pull the returning ark, while the people reaped wheat in the valley?
Where did Jehoash king of Israel defeat and capture Amaziah king of Judah after they 'looked one another in the face'?

name: Kiriath Jearim
note: Identified with the hill of Deir el-Azar above Abu Ghosh, west of Jerusalem.

events.q: At whose town did the ark stay in Abinadab's house for twenty years?

name: Mizpah of Benjamin
note: Mizpah is usually identified with Tell en-Nasbeh north of Jerusalem; Nebi Samwil is an alternative.

events.q: Where did Samuel cast lots before the tribes, choosing Saul, who was found hiding among the baggage?
Where was the governor Gedaliah murdered by Ishmael son of Nethaniah?

name: Ramah
note: Ramah of Benjamin is er-Ram north of Jerusalem; whether Samuel's home Ramathaim-zophim is the same place is debated.

events.q: Where was Samuel's home, to which the elders came demanding a king to judge them like all the nations?
Where was a voice heard of Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted?

name: Bethlehem
note: The Church of the Nativity, among the oldest continuously used churches, stands over the traditional cave of the birth.

events.q: In whose fields did Ruth glean barley behind the reapers of Boaz?
Where did Samuel anoint the youngest of Jesse's sons as king?
Where was Jesus born and laid in a manger?
To which town did the Magi go, following the star, to worship the child?
Near which town, on the road from Bethel, did Rachel die giving birth to Benjamin?

name: Valley of Elah
note: The valley (Wadi es-Sunt) runs past Khirbet Qeiyafa, Socoh, and Azekah in the Judean lowlands.

events.q: In which valley did David kill Goliath with a sling and a stone?

name: Gath
note: Philistine Gath is widely identified with Tell es-Safi (Tel Zafit) in the Judean lowlands.

events.q: Before which Philistine king did David pretend to be insane, scribbling on the gate doors?

name: Ziklag
note: Its location is disputed: Tel Sera' in the northern Negev (pinned here), Tel Halif, and Khirbet a-Ra'i are all proposed.

events.q: Which town did King Achish of Gath give David to live in?
Which town did the Amalekites burn while David was away, carrying off his wives?
Where was David when an Amalekite brought him Saul's crown and armlet?

name: En Gedi
note: En Gedi is an oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea, now a nature reserve and kibbutz.

events.q: In a cave of which wilderness did David secretly cut off the corner of Saul's robe but spare his life?

name: Endor
note: Endor is placed near the former Arab village of Indur and modern Kibbutz Ein Dor, north of the Hill of Moreh.

events.q: Where did Saul consult a medium who called up the spirit of Samuel?

name: Shunem
note: Shunem is the village of Sulam at the foot of the Hill of Moreh in the Jezreel Valley.

events.q: Where did a woman build a small room for Elisha, whose son he later raised from death?
Where did the Philistines encamp before the battle in which Saul died?

name: Mount Gilboa
note: The Gilboa ridge rises southeast of the Jezreel Valley in northern Israel and the West Bank.

events.q: On which mountain did Saul fall on his own sword after his sons were killed by the Philistines?

name: Beth Shean
note: Tel Beth Shean rises above the Roman city of Scythopolis in modern Beit She'an.

events.q: To whose city wall did the Philistines fasten the body of Saul?

name: Jerusalem
note: Jerusalem's Old City and the City of David ridge just south of it preserve the ancient core.

events.q: Which Jebusite stronghold did David capture and make his own city?
Whose walls did Nehemiah rebuild in fifty-two days despite Sanballat's opposition?
Where was the Holy Spirit poured out on the apostles as tongues of fire at Pentecost?
Where did the apostles and elders hold the council that freed Gentile believers from circumcision?
Where did David assemble all Israel to bring up the ark, appointing Asaph, Heman and Ethan to sound bronze cymbals?
In which city did King Jehoiakim cut up the scroll Baruch had written and burn it in the brazier of his winter house?
To which city did Judith go up with the people to worship, dedicating the canopy she had taken from Holofernes' bedchamber?
In which city's Second Quarter did Ahikam, Hilkiah and Shaphan consult the prophetess Huldah about the newly found book?
In which royal city, after David returned from the Ammonite war, did Amnon feign illness and violate his half-sister Tamar?
Into which city was the ark coming when Michal looked out the window and despised David leaping before the LORD?
In which city did King Amon reign two years before his servants killed him in his own house?
In which city, while Joab besieged Rabbah, did David see Bathsheba bathing from his roof?

name: Tekoa
note: Tekoa is Khirbet Tuqu' south of Bethlehem.

events.q: From which town did Joab bring a wise woman to persuade David to bring Absalom home?
Among whose herdsmen was Amos when the LORD called him to prophesy?

name: Dan
note: Tel Dan at the springs of the Jordan preserves a mud-brick gate and the 'House of David' inscription.

events.q: Which northern city was called Laish until a migrating tribe captured it and renamed it after their forefather?
At which northern city, besides Bethel, did Jeroboam set a golden calf?

name: Samaria
note: The royal city of Samaria is the archaeological site at Sebastia, northwest of Nablus.

events.q: Which hill did Omri buy from Shemer to build his new capital?
During the siege of which city were four lepers the first to find the Aramean camp deserted?
To which city did Philip go down to preach Christ, where Simon the sorcerer believed?

name: Jezreel
note: Tel Jezreel overlooks the Jezreel Valley near Kibbutz Yizre'el.

events.q: Where was Naboth stoned so that Ahab could take his vineyard?
Where was Jezebel thrown down from a window and trampled by Jehu's horses?

name: Mount Carmel (El-Muhraqa)
note: The Carmel ridge is certain; the spot of the contest is traditionally El-Muhraqa, marked by a Carmelite monastery.

events.q: Where did Elijah challenge the prophets of Baal, until fire fell from the LORD and consumed his sacrifice?

name: Zarephath
note: Zarephath (Sarepta) is excavated at Sarafand on the Lebanese coast between Tyre and Sidon.

events.q: Where did a widow's jar of flour and jug of oil not run out while she fed Elijah?

name: Tyre
note: Tyre, once an island fortress, is now Sur in southern Lebanon with extensive Roman ruins.

events.q: Whose king sent Solomon cedars and cypress for the Temple?
Where did disciples with wives and children kneel on the beach to pray with Paul before he sailed on?

name: Sidon
note: Sidon is modern Saida in southern Lebanon.

events.q: Of which city's people was Ethbaal king, the father of Jezebel?
Where did the centurion Julius kindly let Paul go to his friends on the first day of his voyage to Rome?

name: Damascus
note: Damascus, the Syrian capital, is among the oldest continuously inhabited cities; Straight Street still crosses its old city.

events.q: Whose rivers, Abana and Pharpar, did Naaman think better than all the waters of Israel?
On which city's Straight Street did Ananias lay hands on Saul so that his sight returned?
From which city's wall was Paul let down in a basket to escape a plot?
Where did King Ahaz go to meet Tiglath-pileser, and copy the design of an altar he saw there?

name: Road to Damascus (Kawkab)
note: Scripture says only that Saul was 'near' the city; a local tradition marks the spot at Kawkab, southwest of Damascus.

events.q: Near which city did a light from heaven flash around Saul and a voice ask, 'Why do you persecute me?'

name: Lachish
note: Tel Lachish is a large excavated mound in the Judean lowlands; Sennacherib's siege is carved on reliefs from Nineveh.

events.q: Which Judean fortress was Sennacherib besieging when Hezekiah sent him tribute and admitted, 'I have offended'?
To which fortress did King Amaziah flee from a conspiracy, only to be pursued and killed there?

name: Anathoth
note: Anathoth lay near the village of Anata northeast of Jerusalem, probably at Ras el-Kharrubeh.

events.q: In his hometown, where did Jeremiah buy his cousin Hanamel's field while Jerusalem was under siege?
To his own fields in which town did Solomon banish Abiathar the priest instead of putting him to death?

name: Modein
note: Modein lay near al-Midya and modern Modi'in; the traditional 'Tombs of the Maccabees' there are not securely identified.

events.q: In which town did Mattathias kill a Jew who came forward to sacrifice to idols, starting the revolt?
Where did Simon build a lofty monument with seven pyramids over the tomb of his father and brothers?

name: Emmaus (Nicopolis)
note: Maccabean Emmaus is Imwas (later Nicopolis) in Canada Park, west of Latrun.

events.q: Near which town did Judas Maccabeus defeat Gorgias's army after a night march?

name: Beth Zur
note: Beth Zur is Khirbet et-Tubeiqa, a hill fortress north of Hebron.

events.q: Where did Judas meet Lysias's army with ten thousand men and defeat it, before rededicating the Temple?

name: Sparta
note: Ancient Sparta's acropolis and theater lie just north of the modern town in the Peloponnese.

events.q: To which Greek people did Jonathan send a letter recalling their kinship with the Jews through Abraham?

name: Nazareth
note: The Basilica of the Annunciation in Nazareth is built over ancient house-caves of the first-century village.

events.q: In which town did the angel Gabriel announce to Mary that she would conceive the Son of the Most High?
In which synagogue did Jesus read from Isaiah, after which the townspeople tried to throw him off a cliff?

name: Cana
note: The traditional site is Kafr Kanna near Nazareth; many archaeologists prefer Khirbet Qana, about 8 km to the north.

events.q: Where did Jesus turn water into wine at a wedding?
Where was Jesus when he told a royal official, 'Go your way. Your son lives'?

name: Nain
note: Nain is the Arab village of Nein below the Hill of Moreh, with a small Franciscan church.

events.q: At the gate of which town did Jesus raise a widow's only son from his funeral bier?

name: Capernaum
note: Capernaum's ruins, with a white limestone synagogue and the traditional house of Peter, lie on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee.

events.q: Where did four men lower a paralyzed man through a roof to Jesus?
In which town did a centurion tell Jesus, 'Lord, I am not worthy for you to come under my roof'?
In which synagogue did Jesus teach, 'I am the bread of life'?

name: Sea of Galilee
note: This freshwater lake in northern Israel, about 21 km long, also goes by Lake Gennesaret or Tiberias.

events.q: Beside which lake did Jesus call Simon and Andrew to become fishers of men?
On which lake did Peter walk on the water toward Jesus, then begin to sink?
On which lake did Jesus rebuke the wind and say to the sea, 'Peace! Be still!'?

name: Mount of Beatitudes
note: Matthew names no mountain; the traditional site is the hill above Tabgha on the northwest shore, crowned by a 1938 church.

events.q: According to tradition, on which hillside did Jesus begin his great sermon with 'Blessed are the poor in spirit'?

name: Bethsaida
note: Bethsaida is usually identified with et-Tell north of the lake, though el-Araj nearer the shore is a strong rival.

events.q: Outside which village did Jesus spit on a blind man's eyes, who first saw people 'like trees walking'?
Which town was home to Philip, Andrew, and Peter?

name: Country of the Gadarenes (Kursi)
note: Manuscripts vary (Gerasenes, Gadarenes, Gergesenes); tradition marks the site at Kursi on the east shore, where a Byzantine monastery stands.

events.q: Where did Jesus cast a legion of demons into a herd of pigs that rushed down a steep bank into the sea?

name: Caesarea Philippi
note: Caesarea Philippi is Banias at the foot of Mount Hermon, beside a cave spring of the Jordan.

events.q: Where did Peter confess, 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God,' and receive the keys of the kingdom?

name: Jacob's Well (Sychar)
note: The well, beneath a Greek Orthodox church at Balata in Nablus, has been venerated since the 4th century and fits John's description.

events.q: At whose well did Jesus ask a Samaritan woman for a drink and speak of living water?

name: Bethany
note: Bethany is al-Eizariya on the east slope of the Mount of Olives, where the traditional tomb of Lazarus is shown.

events.q: Where did Jesus raise Lazarus after he had been four days in the tomb?
In which village did Martha welcome Jesus while her sister sat at his feet listening?

name: Pool of Bethesda
note: The excavated twin pools lie beside the Church of St. Anne near the Lions' Gate in Jerusalem's Old City.

events.q: At which pool with five porches did Jesus heal a man who had been ill for thirty-eight years?

name: Pool of Siloam
note: The first-century pool was uncovered in 2004 at the southern tip of the City of David in Jerusalem.

events.q: In which pool did Jesus send a man born blind to wash the mud from his eyes?

name: Gethsemane
note: Tradition places the garden at the foot of the Mount of Olives, by the Church of All Nations and its ancient olive trees.

events.q: In which garden did Jesus pray, 'Not what I desire, but what you desire,' and was then betrayed with a kiss?

name: Golgotha
note: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre has marked Calvary and the tomb since Constantine's builders identified them in the 4th century.

events.q: Where, at 'the place of a skull,' was Jesus crucified between two criminals?

name: Mount of Olives
note: The ridge east of the Old City, opposite the Temple Mount, is topped by the Chapel of the Ascension.

events.q: From which mount, a Sabbath day's journey from the city, did the apostles watch Jesus taken up into heaven?
Sitting on which hill opposite the Temple did Jesus tell his disciples of the signs of the end of the age?

name: Emmaus (Luke 24)
note: Luke's village, sixty stadia from Jerusalem, is uncertain; candidates include el-Qubeibeh (pinned here, a Franciscan tradition), Motza, Abu Ghosh, and Imwas.

events.q: Toward which village were two disciples walking when the risen Jesus joined them and was known in the breaking of the bread?

name: Lydda
note: Lydda is modern Lod, near Ben Gurion Airport, where the Church of St. George stands.

events.q: Where did Peter heal Aeneas, who had been bedridden for eight years?

name: Joppa
note: Joppa is the old port of Jaffa, now part of Tel Aviv–Yafo.

events.q: From which port did Jonah take a ship to flee from the presence of the LORD?
Where did Peter raise Tabitha (Dorcas) from the dead?
On whose rooftop, at Simon the tanner's house, did Peter see a sheet let down full of animals?

name: Caesarea Maritima
note: Herod's harbor city is a national park on Israel's coast between Tel Aviv and Haifa, with a theater and aqueduct.

events.q: In whose house did the Holy Spirit fall on the centurion Cornelius and his household as Peter preached?
In which city was Herod Agrippa struck by an angel and eaten by worms after accepting worship as a god?
Where was Paul held for two years under Felix before appealing to Caesar before Festus?

name: Antioch (Syria)
note: Syrian Antioch is Antakya in southern Turkey, on the Orontes; the cave church of St. Peter is nearby.

events.q: Where were the disciples first called Christians?
From which church were Barnabas and Saul set apart by the Holy Spirit and sent out on their first mission?
Where did Paul oppose Peter to his face for withdrawing from eating with Gentiles?

name: Tarsus
note: Tarsus is a city in Mersin Province, southern Turkey, where a traditional 'St. Paul's Well' is shown.

events.q: Which city in Cilicia did Paul call home, 'no insignificant city'?
To which city did the brothers send Saul away from Caesarea when the Hellenists sought to kill him?

name: Salamis (Cyprus)
note: The ruins of Salamis lie on the east coast of Cyprus north of Famagusta.

events.q: In which Cypriot port did Barnabas and Saul first proclaim the word in the Jewish synagogues?

name: Paphos
note: Nea Paphos on the southwest coast of Cyprus is a UNESCO site; a column there is traditionally called St. Paul's Pillar.

events.q: Where did Paul strike the sorcerer Elymas blind, so that the proconsul Sergius Paulus believed?

name: Perga
note: Perga's extensive ruins lie near Aksu, east of Antalya in Turkey.

events.q: In which city of Pamphylia did John Mark leave Paul and Barnabas and return to Jerusalem?

name: Antioch of Pisidia
note: The Roman colony's ruins lie beside Yalvaç in Isparta Province, Turkey.

events.q: Where did Paul, rejected by some in the synagogue, declare, 'Behold, we turn to the Gentiles'?

name: Iconium
note: Iconium is Konya, a major city of central Turkey.

events.q: From which city did Paul and Barnabas flee when a plot formed to stone them, after a great number believed?

name: Lystra
note: Lystra is the unexcavated mound of Zoldera near Hatunsaray, identified by a Latin inscription.

events.q: Where did the crowd call Barnabas 'Zeus' and Paul 'Hermes' after Paul healed a lame man?
In which town was Paul stoned and dragged out of the city, left for dead?
Where did Paul meet Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father?

name: Troas
note: Alexandria Troas is a ruined port on Turkey's Aegean coast, south of ancient Troy.

events.q: Where did Paul see a vision of a man of Macedonia pleading, 'Come over into Macedonia and help us'?
Where did the young man Eutychus fall asleep during Paul's long talk and fall from a third-story window?

name: Ephesus
note: Ephesus is a major excavated city near Selçuk, Turkey, with a great theater that seated about 25,000.

events.q: Where did Demetrius the silversmith stir up a riot, with the crowd shouting 'Great is Artemis' in the theater?
Where did those who practiced magic burn their books, worth fifty thousand pieces of silver?
Which church did the risen Christ tell, 'You have left your first love'?

name: Miletus
note: The ruins of Miletus, including a great theater, lie near Balat on Turkey's Aegean coast; the harbor has silted far inland.

events.q: Where did Paul summon the Ephesian elders and bid them a tearful farewell, saying they would see his face no more?

name: Patmos
note: Patmos is a Greek island in the Dodecanese; the Cave of the Apocalypse is shown below the Monastery of St. John.

events.q: On which island was John 'because of God's Word' when he received the Revelation?

name: Smyrna
note: Smyrna is modern İzmir, Turkey, where the Roman agora has been excavated.

events.q: Which church did the risen Christ tell, 'Be faithful to death, and I will give you the crown of life'?

name: Pergamum
note: Pergamum's acropolis towers over modern Bergama, Turkey; its great altar of Zeus is now in Berlin.

events.q: Which church lived 'where Satan's throne is,' where the faithful witness Antipas was killed?

name: Thyatira
note: Thyatira is modern Akhisar, Turkey, with a small excavated area in the town center.

events.q: Which city was home to Lydia, the seller of purple cloth?
Which church was rebuked for tolerating 'that woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess'?

name: Sardis
note: Sardis, the old Lydian capital, is excavated at Sart, Turkey, with a restored gymnasium and large synagogue.

events.q: Which church was told, 'You have a reputation of being alive, but you are dead'?

name: Philadelphia
note: Philadelphia is modern Alaşehir, Turkey, where pillars of a Byzantine church survive.

events.q: Which church was told, 'I have set before you an open door, which no one can shut'?

name: Laodicea
note: Laodicea on the Lycus is an excavated site near Denizli, Turkey.

events.q: Which church was rebuked as lukewarm, neither hot nor cold?

name: Philippi
note: Philippi is a UNESCO site in northeastern Greece, near Kavala.

events.q: Where did Lydia and her household become the first baptized converts in Europe, by a riverside place of prayer?
Where did an earthquake open the prison doors at midnight, after which the jailer was baptized?

name: Thessalonica
note: Thessalonica is Thessaloniki, Greece's second city, with a Roman forum and Galerius's arch.

events.q: Where did a mob attack Jason's house, accusing Paul's companions of 'turning the world upside down'?

name: Berea
note: Berea is modern Veria in Macedonia, Greece, where a shrine marks the traditional spot of Paul's preaching.

events.q: Where did the Jews receive the word eagerly and examine the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so?

name: Athens (Areopagus)
note: The Areopagus is a rocky hill just northwest of the Acropolis in central Athens.

events.q: Where did Paul preach about an altar 'to an unknown god,' and Dionysius and Damaris believed?

name: Corinth
note: Ancient Corinth's ruins, with the Temple of Apollo and the bema, lie southwest of the modern city.

events.q: Where did Paul work as a tentmaker with Aquila and Priscilla, newly arrived from Italy?
Where did the proconsul Gallio refuse to judge the charges brought against Paul?

name: Cenchreae
note: Cenchreae was Corinth's eastern port; its submerged harbor remains lie near modern Kechries.

events.q: Where did Paul shave his head because of a vow before sailing for Syria?
Of which church was Phoebe, whom Paul commends to the Romans, a servant?

name: Fair Havens (Crete)
note: Fair Havens is Kaloi Limenes, a small bay on the south coast of Crete that still bears the name.

events.q: In which harbor near Lasea did Paul warn that sailing on would bring disaster, but was overruled?

name: Malta (St. Paul's Bay)
note: The island is securely Malta; the exact shipwreck spot is uncertain and is traditionally placed at St. Paul's Bay on the north coast.

events.q: On which island did Paul survive a shipwreck and shake off a viper into the fire unharmed?
Where did Paul heal the father of Publius, the chief official of the island, of fever?

name: Puteoli
note: Puteoli is modern Pozzuoli on the Bay of Naples, Italy.

events.q: At which Italian port did Paul find brothers who invited him to stay seven days?

name: Rome
note: Rome, capital of Italy, holds the tombs of Peter and Paul at St. Peter's Basilica and St. Paul Outside the Walls.

events.q: Where did Paul live two whole years in his own rented house, preaching the kingdom of God unhindered?
From which city did Claudius expel all the Jews, including Aquila and Priscilla?

name: Tarshish
note: Tarshish is uncertain; it is often linked with Tartessos in southwestern Spain (pinned near Huelva), though some scholars propose Sardinia or elsewhere.

events.q: Where was Jonah's ship headed when he fled from the presence of the LORD?

name: Sheba (Marib)
note: Sheba is usually identified with the kingdom of Saba in Yemen, whose capital Marib preserves temple ruins; some traditions favor Ethiopia instead.

events.q: From which kingdom did a queen come to test Solomon with hard questions?

name: Cyrene
note: Cyrene is a UNESCO-listed Greek city at Shahhat in eastern Libya.

events.q: Which city was home to the man compelled to carry Jesus' cross, the father of Alexander and Rufus?

name: Mount Hor
note: Scripture sets Mount Hor on the border of Edom; since Josephus tradition has placed it at Jebel Harun above Petra, crowned by a shrine to Aaron, though some scholars prefer a peak nearer Kadesh.

events.q: On which mountain did Moses strip Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar before Aaron died?

name: Riblah
note: Riblah 'in the land of Hamath' is identified with the village of Ribleh on the Orontes in western Syria, near the Lebanese border.

events.q: In which town in the land of Hamath did the king of Babylon kill Zedekiah's sons before his eyes and then blind him?

name: Mareshah
note: Tel Maresha, in the Judean lowlands beside Beit Guvrin, is an excavated mound honeycombed with Hellenistic caves.

events.q: Where did King Asa cry to the LORD and defeat the vast army of Zerah the Ethiopian in the valley of Zephathah?

name: Megiddo
note: Tel Megiddo commands the pass into the Jezreel Valley; its name lies behind 'Armageddon' (Har Megiddo).

events.q: Where was King Josiah killed when he went out against Pharaoh Necoh?

name: Gihon Spring
note: The Gihon spring in the Kidron Valley below the City of David was Jerusalem's main water source and still flows into Hezekiah's Tunnel.

events.q: To which spring did Zadok, Nathan and Benaiah bring Solomon on David's mule to anoint him king?

name: En Rogel
note: En Rogel is usually identified with Bir Ayyub ('Job's Well') where the Kidron and Hinnom valleys meet south of the City of David.

events.q: By which spring did Adonijah sacrifice at the stone of Zoheleth and feast his supporters to proclaim himself king?
By which spring outside the city did Ahimaaz and Jonathan wait for news to carry to David during Absalom's revolt?

name: Keilah
note: Keilah is Khirbet Qila, a hilltop ruin in the Shephelah northwest of Hebron that preserves the ancient name.

events.q: To which town, which David had just saved from the Philistines, did Abiathar flee carrying an ephod?

name: Baal Hazor
note: Usually identified with Jebel 'Asur (Tell Asur), the high hill northeast of Bethel near Ephraim (et-Taiyibeh).

events.q: At which place near Ephraim did Absalom's servants kill Amnon during the sheep-shearing feast?

name: Shittim (Abel Shittim)
note: Israel's last camp on the plains of Moab; often located at Tell el-Hammam, though nearby Tell Kefrein is another candidate.

events.q: At which camp in the plains of Moab did Phinehas stop the plague by spearing Zimri and the Midianite Cozbi?

name: Zorah
note: Tel Tzora, on the ridge above the Sorek Valley near Kibbutz Tzora, preserves the name of Samson's hometown.

events.q: In which Danite town did the angel of the LORD appear to Manoah's barren wife, promising her a son?
